title: 第十三章 仓库第十四章 第一笔分红
lines: 钥匙在兜里揣了三天，沈南枝没动。
不是不想动，是腾不出手。订单压着，新招的三个女工还得手把手教，高端产品的那几件样品要在月底之前做完寄给周志豪过目，店里的账本她三天没碰了，抽屉里塞了一堆送货单没对。
每天的活儿排得满满当当的，连上厕所都是小跑着去的。
第四天早上，她比平时早起了半个钟头。外头天还没大亮，灰蒙蒙的，对面修车铺的灯已经亮了。她站在窗户后面看了一眼，陆沉舟蹲在门口刷牙，一手端着搪瓷缸子，一手拿着牙刷，刷得满嘴白沫。
她拉上窗帘，换了件旧衣裳，出门了。
仓库在修车铺隔壁，同一排房子，中间隔了两家店面。她走过去的时候经过修车铺，陆沉舟已经刷完牙了，正在往脸上泼冷水，听见脚步声扭头看了一眼，点了下头，没说话。
沈南枝没停，走到仓库门口，掏出那把钥匙。
锁是老式的挂锁，铜的，有点锈，插钥匙的时候卡了一下，她使劲拧了两下才开。卷帘门推上去的时候哗啦一声响，灰尘从门头上落下来，呛得她往后退了一步，捂着嘴咳了两声。
里面的灯绳拉了一下没拉到，又往前摸了两步才够着。灯亮了，是一盏白炽灯，瓦数不大，昏黄昏黄的，照得整个仓库半明半暗。
仓库不大，二十来平方，地面是水泥的，墙上刷的白灰起皮了，地面上堆着几个纸箱和一卷旧帆布。靠里的墙根有一张铁架床，上面铺着一层薄褥子，叠得整整齐齐的，被子是军绿色的，洗得发白，枕头上搭着一条叠成方块的毛巾。
床头的地上放着两个暖水瓶，一个搪瓷盆，盆里搁着肥皂和牙刷。
锅碗瓢盆挨着墙角摞着，用一块旧布盖着。旁边是用砖头垒的一个简易灶台，上面搁着一口小铁锅，锅盖盖着。
沈南枝蹲下来，把盖锅的布掀开一条缝。锅里还剩下半锅白水面条，汤没了，面条坨成一团，上面凝了一层白花花的油。
她往灶台旁边看了一眼，地上搁着几个瓶瓶罐罐——盐、酱油、醋，没了。
她把布盖回去，站起来，在仓库里又转了一圈。
床底下有两双鞋，一双解放鞋，鞋帮子上全是泥点子，另一双是黑布鞋，鞋底磨得薄了，后跟快通了。床头的木箱子上放着几本书，摞着，最上面那本翻了一半，扣着放在那里。
她走过去拿起来看了看，是一本《摩托车维修技术》，书页发黄，边角卷了，里面夹着一张旧报纸当书签。底下的几本更旧，封面的字都快磨没了。
她把书放回原处。
角落里的纸箱开着口，她往里瞅了一眼，全是修车用的零件——火花塞、刹车片、链条什么的，分门别类用小盒子装着，箱子上贴了标签，字写得端端正正的。
她把仓库的门窗都打开了，让空气流通一下。太阳已经出来了，光线从门口照进来，把满地的灰尘照得清清楚楚。
桂姨不知道什么时候过来的，站在门口往里看，看了一圈，叹了口气。
“这小伙子，一个人住在这里？”桂姨的声音压得很低，“连个正经厨房都没有。”
沈南枝没接话。
“你看见那锅面没？”桂姨说，“剩了半锅，昨晚上吃的，早上又接着吃。天天就吃这个，白水煮面，连个鸡蛋都不舍得放。”
“他放了。”沈南枝说。
桂姨愣了一下：“放了？放了什么？”
桂姨被她这个冷幽默弄愣了，回过神来，又好气又好笑地瞪了她一眼：“你这孩子，我跟你说正经的。”
沈南枝把窗户推开，让风吹进来。仓库外面是条窄巷子，堆着一些杂物，墙角长了几棵野草，叶子被露水打湿了，绿得发亮。
“姨，这仓库我用了。”她说，“把货柜搬过来，加工点设在这边，店里就只卖货，不占地方。”
“那对面的——”桂姨话说了一半，咽回去了。
沈南枝没解释。
“你去帮我把隔壁楼张嫂叫过来，”她说，“上次她说想来干活，我答应她了。让她今天就来，先把仓库收拾出来。”
桂姨点了点头，转身去了。
沈南枝一个人站在仓库里，又看了一圈。
这地方当加工点，位置合适，离店里近，搬货方便。就是得收拾——得刷墙，得加货架，得装灯，得多接几个插座，得把灶台那边隔开，不能跟加工区混在一起。
她心里盘算着这些，手上也没闲着，把那卷旧帆布卷起来搬到门口，把地上的纸箱重新摞好，又拿扫帚把地扫了一遍。
扫到床底下的时候，扫出来一个烟头。
content_en:
The key had been in his pocket for three days, but Shen Nanzhi didn't move it.
It's not that I don't want to move, it's that I can't move. Orders were being pressed, and the three newly recruited female workers had to teach them step by step. The few samples of high-end products had to be completed and sent to Zhou Zhihao for review before the end of the month. She hadn't touched the store's account book for three days, and there was a pile of delivery orders stuffed in the drawer.
The daily schedule of work is so full that even going to the toilet has to be done at a trot.
On the morning of the fourth day, she got up half an hour earlier than usual. It was still dark outside and it was gray, but the lights of the car repair shop opposite were already on. She stood behind the window and took a look. Lu Chenzhou was squatting at the door brushing his teeth, holding an enamel basin in one hand and a toothbrush in the other, brushing his mouth full of foam.
She closed the curtains, changed into some old clothes, and went out.
The warehouse is next to the car repair shop, in the same row of houses, with two stores separated in the middle. When she walked over, she passed the car repair shop. Lu Chenzhou had already finished brushing his teeth and was pouring cold water on his face. When he heard the footsteps, he turned his head and glanced, nodded, and said nothing.
Shen Nanzhi didn't stop, walked to the door of the warehouse and took out the key.
The lock was an old-fashioned padlock, made of copper and a little rusty. When she inserted the key, it got stuck. She turned it hard twice before opening it. There was a loud crash when the rolling shutter door was pushed up, and dust fell from the top of the door. She was choked and took a step back, covering her mouth and coughing twice.
I pulled the light cord inside but couldn't reach it, so I took two more steps forward to reach it. The light was on. It was an incandescent lamp with a small wattage and a dim glow, illuminating the entire warehouse in half-light and half-darkness.
The warehouse is not big, about twenty square meters. The floor is made of cement. The white plaster on the walls is peeling. There are several cardboard boxes and a roll of old canvas piled on the floor. There was an iron frame bed against the inner wall, with a thin mattress on it, neatly folded. The quilt was military green and washed white, and there was a towel folded into a square on the pillow.
On the floor beside the bed were two thermos bottles and an enamel basin with soap and a toothbrush in it.
Pots and pans were stacked against the wall, covered with an old cloth. Next to it is a simple stove made of bricks, with a small iron pot covered with a lid.
Shen Nanzhi squatted down and opened a crack in the cloth covering the pot. There was still half a pot of plain water noodles left in the pot. The soup was gone and the noodles were lumpy with a layer of white oil on them.
She glanced at the stove. There were several bottles and jars on the floor - the salt, soy sauce, and vinegar were all gone.
She put the cloth back on, stood up, and walked around the warehouse again.
There are two pairs of shoes under the bed, one pair of Jiefang shoes with mud spots all over the uppers, and the other pair of black cloth shoes with worn-out soles and almost broken heels. There were several books stacked on the wooden box beside the bed. The top one was half opened and buckled there.
She walked over and picked it up and looked at it. It was a book called "Motorcycle Maintenance Technology". The pages were yellowed and the corners were curled. There was an old newspaper inside as a bookmark. The books at the bottom are older, and the words on the covers are almost worn away.
She put the book back where it belonged.
The cardboard box in the corner was open, and she glanced inside. They were all parts for car repairs—spark plugs, brake pads, chains, etc. They were sorted into small boxes, and the boxes were labeled and written neatly.
She opened the doors and windows of the warehouse to let some air circulate. The sun has come out, and the light shines in through the door, clearly illuminating the dust on the floor.
Aunt Gui didn't know when she came over. She stood at the door and looked in. She looked around and sighed.
"This young man lives here alone?" Aunt Gui's voice was very low, "There isn't even a proper kitchen."
Shen Nanzhi didn't answer.
"Have you seen that pot of noodles?" Aunt Gui said, "There is half a pot left. I ate it last night and started eating it again in the morning. I eat this every day, boiled noodles in plain water, and I don't even want to put an egg in it."
"He let it go," Shen Nanzhi said.
Aunt Gui was stunned for a moment: "Let it go? What did it let go?"
"Vinegar."
Aunt Gui was stunned by her cold humor. When she came to her senses, she glared at her angrily and funnyly: "You kid, I'm telling you to be serious."
Shen Nanzhi opened the window and let the wind blow in. Outside the warehouse is a narrow alley with some debris piled up, and a few weeds growing in the corners. The leaves are wet with dew and are shiny green.
"Auntie, I'm using this warehouse," she said. "Move the containers over here and set up the processing point here. The store will only sell goods and won't take up any space."
"Then on the other side -" Aunt Gui said half of her words before swallowing it back.
Shen Nanzhi didn't explain.
"Go and help me call Sister-in-law Zhang from the building next door," she said. "Last time she said she wanted to come and work, and I agreed to her. Let her come today and clean up the warehouse first."
Aunt Gui nodded and turned around.
Shen Nanzhi stood alone in the warehouse and looked around again.
This place is used as a processing point. The location is suitable, close to the store, and easy to move goods. It just has to be tidied up - the walls have to be painted, shelves have to be added, lights have to be installed, a few more sockets have to be connected, and the stove side has to be separated so that it cannot be mixed with the processing area.
She was thinking about this in her mind, and her hands were not idle. She rolled up the old canvas and moved it to the door, re-stacked the cardboard boxes on the floor, and swept the floor again with a broom handle.
When I swept under the bed, I found a cigarette butt.
title_en: Chapter Thirteen Warehouse Chapter Fourteen The First Dividend
